entry.title: The evasive evitability of enshittification
entry.summary: Our company recently announced a fundraise. We were grateful for all the community support, but the Internet also raised a few of its collective eyebrows, wondering whether this meant the dreaded “enshittification” was coming next. That word describes a very real pattern we’ve all seen before: products start great, grow fast, and then slowly become worse as the people running them trade user love for short-term revenue. It’s a topic I find genuinely fascinating, and I've seen the downward spiral firsthand at companies I once admired. So I want to talk about why this happens, and more importantly, why it won't happen to us. That's big talk, I know. But it's a promise I'm happy for people to hold us to. What is enshittification?
